events.title: The Depths Are Awakening!
events.summary: Hello, Architects! 🏰Steam Next Fest is underway, and while some adventurers are still trying to survive the demo, I've been busy working on content for the full game.This time, I decided to explore two very different settings: the depths of the abyss and a pirate tavern.After all, even pirates need somewhere to grab a drink. And sea monsters deserve a home too.But before I show you what's new, there's something I want to officially confirm:Fame & Fear: Dungeon Architect will launch in version 1.

events.title: Cursed Carnival & 10 New Traps: Let the Show Begin!
events.summary: Hello, Architects!The dungeon already had monsters, traps, and a questionable approach to safety. What it was missing was clowns.This update introduces Cursed Carnival, a new theme featuring decorations, building pieces, and two creatures ready to take charge of the entertainment. events.title: Your Dungeon Comes Alive! New Strategies, Keeper's Orders & the Grand Expedition
events.summary: Hello, Architects! Over the past few days, we've been working on one of the biggest updates yet for Fame & Fear: Dungeon Architect.Our goal was simple: make every decision matter and turn your dungeon into a place that truly reacts to the choices you make.We've introduced new tools to plan your days, understand adventurer behavior, intervene during visits, and discover which strategies actually work.But that's not all! events.title: More Room for Your Dungeon: UI, Inns, and Combat Update
events.summary: Hello, architects!This update focuses on how you build, manage, and watch your dungeon. I’ve reorganized the interface to leave more room for the game itself, expanded the furniture you can use in inns, and worked on animations and effects to make adventurers’ and monsters’ actions easier to follow.There are also changes to admission spending, rank promotion costs, and daily reports. events.title: Hey... Max is here!

events.title: Blueprint Workshop – Small Demo Fix
events.summary: A small update regarding the Blueprint system.Due to a Steam limitation, Blueprints created in the Demo cannot currently be published to the Steam Workshop.For this reason, I’ve disabled the Publish to Workshop button in the Demo to avoid confusion.You can still create, save and reuse your Blueprint rooms normally.The full version will retain Steam Workshop publishing support.Thanks for the reports!

events.title: He has a skeleton in the closet... literally!

I’m not here to judge.I’ve also introduced the first themed pack: the Necromancer Pack is here.
